title: Leading the brass band for the 1947 film
summary: Howard led a twelve-man brass band for a funeral scene in the 1947 New Orleans film, with a list of personnel and tunes.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: He was in the 40s and sometimes. George played with me for the picture in 47 when we made the picture in New Orleans.

I had the brass band. I represented Louis Armstrong when he was doing the picture, do you know what it means, Miss New Orleans? I had the band in Al Jays. I did the funeral part on Saturday. And they had artificial coughing, preaching at the club. The Young Men of Al Jays Club, they had the club in the old time carriage and so forth. It's like a real funeral. They had a real funeral marches. And the next day we left the cemetery with the parade like you usually do, dancing and all that sort of thing. Which they never showed, but I don't know what they did with it, but anyway it was dead.
I had Big Jim, Bill Matthews, Little Jim, Cindy Brown. I had Louis the Man, Old Man Allen, Trumpet. I had Arthur Hogan, John Baptiste.

That's Bat Mosley. John Mosley, that's his right name, but we call him Bat Mosley. And I had Howard Davis, I think he was to play, but something had happened that he couldn't, so Howard Davis played the clarinet, and George Lewis. No saxophone?

I got all that on that sketch when I sent him to England. I know there was twelve of us, that's for sure. But the brass was Big Jim and Bill Matthews, and Old Man Allen, and Louis, and myself. It was twelve men. What numbers did you play? Do you remember? Well we played for a few of them, Flea's Abide. That was the few of them we played at the cemetery. The next day we played the blues and different other numbers, St. Louis blues and something else. From Night Down, a real cemetery, back to Algae. We took the society. Mm-hmm. Where all have you been at the cemetery? Yeah. We took the society. Where all have you been at the cemetery? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. We took the society. Mm-hmm. That was the film we played at the cemetery. The next day, well, we played the blues and different other numbers, St. Louis blues and something else. From Night Down, a real cemetery, back to Algae's. We took the society. Mm-hmm. Where all have you been with George?
